development area: Metadata and machine-actionable output quality assurance
description: Ability to review and validate structured metadata, API-facing output definitions, open-format dissemination files, and AI-generated output templates for completeness, consistency, usability, and standards compliance.
historic work: Key Activities: Edits, validates, markets and disseminates data.
change to work: This activity will expand beyond validating final human-readable products to validating standardized dissemination packages, metadata completeness, machine-actionable structures, API-ready outputs, and open-format delivery objects. Marketing and dissemination will increasingly rely on discoverability, interoperability, and metadata quality rather than only traditional publication or release practices.
justification: The current wording emphasizes editing, validation, marketing, and dissemination of data, but not validation of machine-actionable dissemination products, metadata structures, or automated output-generation workflows.

description: Knowledge of dissemination standards, open data formats, API concepts, metadata tagging conventions, and interoperability principles for reuse by both human and machine clients.
historic work: Key Activities: Edits, validates, markets and disseminates data.
change to work: This activity will expand beyond validating final human-readable products to validating standardized dissemination packages, metadata completeness, machine-actionable structures, API-ready outputs, and open-format delivery objects. Marketing and dissemination will increasingly rely on discoverability, interoperability, and metadata quality rather than only traditional publication or release practices.
justification: The update requires outputs to support APIs, open formats, and interoperability, which is not explicit in the current role expectations.

description: Ability to assess client requests against existing products, self-service options, API access pathways, and organizational criteria for when custom outputs or visualizations are justified.
historic work: Key Activities: Interprets client information requests to create custom statistical tabulations.
change to work: Client request interpretation will now include deciding whether a custom tabulation or visualization is necessary at all, or whether the need can be met through self-service tools, standardized outputs, APIs, or existing products. The role will need to assess user value and the appropriateness of different output forms earlier in the request cycle.
justification: The future role requires evaluating whether a request should result in a custom output, a reusable machine-readable product, a self-service path, or no new product at all.

description: Knowledge of criteria for selecting, simplifying, or omitting dissemination products based on user value, compliance obligations, accessibility, and operational efficiency.
historic work: Key Activities: Interprets client information requests to create custom statistical tabulations.
change to work: Client request interpretation will now include deciding whether a custom tabulation or visualization is necessary at all, or whether the need can be met through self-service tools, standardized outputs, APIs, or existing products. The role will need to assess user value and the appropriateness of different output forms earlier in the request cycle.
justification: The updated process explicitly includes early review of the type and necessity of products, especially visualizations.

description: Ability to test and evaluate outputs produced by automated and AI-supported systems, including template accuracy, metadata generation quality, dissemination configuration logic, and error detection.
historic work: Key Activities: Reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases.
change to work: Quality review will broaden from data and system outputs to include AI-supported output templates, metadata generated automatically, dissemination configurations, and machine-readable product integrity. The officer will need to assess whether automated systems are producing outputs that are statistically accurate, appropriately described, and reusable.
justification: The update introduces automated and AI-supported output design, which requires new forms of review beyond conventional data quality checks.

development area: AI-assisted output generation risks and controls
description: Knowledge of common failure modes, bias/error risks, validation methods, and governance controls associated with AI-supported output and metadata generation.
historic work: Key Activities: Reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases.
change to work: Quality review will broaden from data and system outputs to include AI-supported output templates, metadata generated automatically, dissemination configurations, and machine-readable product integrity. The officer will need to assess whether automated systems are producing outputs that are statistically accurate, appropriately described, and reusable.
justification: The current role includes reviewing computer systems and databases, but not specifically AI-assisted design outputs or metadata automation risks.

description: Ability to explain and support user access through metadata-rich products, self-service tools, APIs, and open formats, while matching dissemination methods to user needs.
historic work: Key Activities: Provides statistical data and consultative services to users.
change to work: Consultative services will increasingly involve advising users on standardized products, metadata-rich outputs, machine-readable access methods, API or self-service options, and the appropriateness of alternative dissemination forms instead of only supplying direct statistical outputs.
justification: The consultative dimension of the role must evolve to explain digital dissemination options and guide users toward interoperable and self-serve access pathways.

description: Ability to work effectively with technical, methodological, metadata, confidentiality, and external partner teams in standardized digital dissemination environments.
historic work: Key Activities: Participates on data production and dissemination teams.
change to work: Team participation will involve stronger collaboration with metadata specialists, dissemination platform staff, API/service designers, confidentiality reviewers, and external partners to ensure outputs align with standards and digital-to-digital workflows.
justification: The update increases the number and diversity of design stakeholders, including external partners and technical dissemination functions.

development area: Operational guidance for modern dissemination practices
description: Knowledge of emerging dissemination workflows, metadata standards, and automated output-design practices sufficient to contribute to staff training and job aids.
historic work: Key Activities: Provides input to training material and assists in the delivery.
change to work: Training contributions will need to cover automated output-design tools, metadata expectations, open-format dissemination, machine-actionable outputs, and criteria for selecting or omitting visualizations and custom products.
justification: The updated dissemination model introduces new practices that must be communicated internally through training and guidance materials.

description: Ability to convert user, subject-matter, and program requirements into structured output, metadata, interoperability, and dissemination tool specifications.
historic work: Communication: Liaises with other specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development and to suggest improvements to ongoing programs.
change to work: Liaison work will increasingly include translating user and subject-matter needs into specifications for standardized metadata, API-ready outputs, machine-readable dissemination structures, and automated template/configuration requirements. Communication must bridge business needs and digital dissemination design standards.
justification: The existing communication expectation covers system development generally, but not the specificity of machine-actionable dissemination and metadata specifications.

description: Ability to prepare publication and dissemination text that aligns with metadata structures, discoverability requirements, and reusable digital documentation practices.
historic work: Communication: Drafts reports and articles on the interpretation and use of statistical data and the concepts, methods and techniques used. These reports and articles are reviewed by program managers and are included in publications.
change to work: Drafting work will need to support more standardized and metadata-enriched products, with clearer explanation of methods, limitations, and machine-readable access points. Written products may also become more modular and structured to support discoverability and reuse.
justification: The update requires outputs and dissemination artifacts to be richly described and machine-actionable, implying more structured descriptive content than traditional reports alone.

development area: Training content development for digital workflows
description: Ability to create and deliver training on standardized dissemination processes, metadata requirements, automation tools, and QA checkpoints for modern outputs.
historic work: Communication: Drafts program information manuals and training packages for use by colleagues, operational staff and management, and assists in the delivery of training.
change to work: Training materials will require coverage of automated and AI-supported dissemination design, metadata generation/validation, API and open-format concepts, and decision criteria for output necessity.
justification: Existing training support does not explicitly require literacy in automated dissemination design or metadata-driven publication practices.

development area: Feasibility assessment for modern dissemination models
description: Knowledge of how dissemination design choices affect operational sustainability, user access, automation potential, and product necessity.
historic work: 4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of methods, techniques, practices and procedures to prepare information for studies and to review the feasibility and potential impact of new or modified statistical programs.
change to work: Feasibility review will now include the practicality of delivering products through standardized, automated, and machine-readable dissemination channels, as well as evaluating whether certain products should be replaced by self-service or API access.
justification: The update changes what 'feasibility' means by incorporating digital dissemination methods and product rationalization decisions.

description: Knowledge of how statistical concepts, classifications, and methods must be represented consistently across metadata, dissemination formats, APIs, and automated outputs.
historic work: 4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of the socio-economic concepts and methods to assess the validity of collected and processed data, the output from computer applications, the validity of database contents and results from alternative manipulations of data.
change to work: Assessment of output validity will need to include whether automated dissemination products and metadata accurately reflect the data and methods, and whether alternative machine-readable presentations preserve statistical meaning.
justification: The current knowledge statement addresses outputs from computer applications generally, but not metadata integrity and machine-readable statistical representation.

development area: Use of modern dissemination and automation tools
description: Ability to use contemporary tools for metadata management, automated template generation, dissemination configuration, structured output validation, and related digital workflows.
historic work: 4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of analytical software for micro-computers.
change to work: The technology expectation is outdated relative to AI-supported output design and modern dissemination tooling. The role will require familiarity with automation-enabled dissemination platforms, metadata tools, and possibly low-code or scripted validation environments.
justification: Current knowledge of analytical software for micro-computers is insufficient for AI-supported, standardized dissemination design environments.

description: Knowledge of internal standards, governance expectations, and policy directions related to metadata quality, automation, open formats, APIs, and digital dissemination design.
historic work: 5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of the divisional mandate, objectives, programs, policies and activities to adhere to the various statistical and administrative practices and procedures involved in the editing, validation, marketing and dissemination of statistical data.
change to work: Contextual knowledge must now include organizational standards for machine-actionable dissemination, automation use, metadata richness, self-service provision, and output minimization where appropriate.
justification: The updated process introduces new operational expectations that are policy- and standards-driven, not just procedural.

description: Knowledge of how to identify and align reusable output structures, metadata patterns, and dissemination conventions across statistical domains.
historic work: 5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of data sources within Statistics Canada in order to locate, analyze and compare related statistical output to ensure consistency and reliability.
change to work: This knowledge will need to extend from comparing statistical outputs to comparing metadata, standardized output structures, and interoperable dissemination artifacts across programs for consistency and reuse.
justification: The future role requires consistency not only in data outputs but also in metadata and reusable dissemination patterns across sources.

description: Knowledge of how confidentiality, privacy, disclosure control, and access restrictions must be embedded in automated outputs, metadata, APIs, and standardized dissemination products from the design stage onward.
historic work: 5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts such as the Corporate Returns Act and Income Tax Act, and of Statistics Canada policies to ensure understanding and application in the editing, validation, marketing and dissemination of data. The position must have a particular awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data to ensure their own actions are in compliance.
change to work: Confidentiality obligations will remain central but will need to be applied earlier in output design, including in automated templates, metadata publication, API exposure, and decisions about what dissemination artifacts should exist at all.
justification: The update explicitly incorporates confidentiality into early output design and applies it to machine-readable dissemination artifacts.

description: Ability to determine the most appropriate dissemination form—including whether no bespoke chart or visualization is needed—while preserving interpretability, consistency, and user value.
historic work: 6. Research and analysis: Compiles data from diverse sources to produce statistical charts, tables and other output. Summarizes and describes meaning of data. Analyzes and evaluates data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness.
change to work: This activity will evolve from producing charts and tables directly toward validating whether such outputs are required, ensuring output forms are standardized and machine-readable where appropriate, and verifying that metadata and descriptions support correct interpretation and reuse.
justification: The update introduces a requirement to evaluate necessity of visualizations and to support machine-actionable output forms.

description: Knowledge of how changes in AI, automation tools, metadata systems, and digital service models affect statistical products, workflows, and user experience.
historic work: 6. Research and analysis: Analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services.
change to work: Analysis will increasingly focus on the effects of automation, AI-supported output design, metadata generation, and interoperability requirements on dissemination products and client services.
justification: The role already includes change analysis, but the technological scope now includes AI and digital dissemination infrastructure.

description: Knowledge of how dissemination systems, metadata repositories, APIs, and partner-facing digital workflows connect with upstream statistical processing environments.
historic work: 6. Research and analysis: Examines operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions with other divisional systems.
change to work: System examination will need to consider integration with dissemination platforms, metadata repositories, APIs, and external digital workflows, not only internal data capture and processing systems.
justification: The updated process emphasizes alignment with digital-to-digital workflows and standards, broadening system integration requirements.

description: Ability to assess and compare dissemination options across publications, tabulations, APIs, metadata-enabled discovery, and self-service mechanisms.
historic work: 6. Research and analysis: Interprets user requests to determine the nature, feasibility, and options for providing the information required.
change to work: Interpretation of requests will now include deciding among existing outputs, APIs, self-service tools, machine-readable products, custom tables, or non-production of new artifacts where alternatives suffice.
justification: This is the analytical counterpart to client service change and requires a broader decision framework than traditional request fulfillment.

development area: Data transformation for open and interoperable dissemination
description: Ability to prepare data and associated descriptions for standardized, reusable, open, and machine-readable dissemination formats.
historic work: 6. Research and analysis: Adapts data to new definitions or presentation formats, depending on the complexity of the subject matter or the number of different sources.
change to work: Adaptation work will now include transforming data into standardized open formats, metadata-tagged structures, and machine-consumable presentations while preserving meaning and comparability.
justification: The update requires open formats and machine-actionable outputs, which extends the concept of 'presentation formats' substantially.

description: Knowledge of how modular dissemination components, automated publication workflows, dynamic output generation, and API-based delivery operate so the officer can validate, monitor, and support automated release processes.
historic work: Key Activities - Edits, validates, markets and disseminates data.
change to work: This activity expands from direct dissemination of finished products to validating and overseeing automated dissemination pipelines and modular release components. 'Disseminates data' now includes assuring readiness of machine-actionable outputs, checking versioning and metadata completeness, supporting automated updates across channels, and intervening when automation produces errors, inconsistencies, or policy risks. Marketing-related activity also shifts toward ensuring discoverability and usability of open data, APIs, and dynamic dissemination products rather than primarily traditional publication formats.
justification: Current wording emphasizes editing, validation, marketing, and dissemination of statistical data, but does not explicitly require operating within automated, API-enabled, metadata-driven dissemination environments.

development area: Metadata and version control for dissemination
description: Knowledge of dissemination metadata standards, release versioning practices, auditability requirements, and how metadata supports discoverability, interoperability, and consistent automated publication.
historic work: Key Activities - Edits, validates, markets and disseminates data.
change to work: This activity expands from direct dissemination of finished products to validating and overseeing automated dissemination pipelines and modular release components. 'Disseminates data' now includes assuring readiness of machine-actionable outputs, checking versioning and metadata completeness, supporting automated updates across channels, and intervening when automation produces errors, inconsistencies, or policy risks. Marketing-related activity also shifts toward ensuring discoverability and usability of open data, APIs, and dynamic dissemination products rather than primarily traditional publication formats.
justification: The update introduces versioning, metadata enrichment, and machine-actionable outputs as standard dissemination requirements not explicitly reflected in the current role.

development area: Automated dissemination QA and exception handling
description: Skill in testing automated outputs, identifying release anomalies, tracing errors across dissemination channels, and making decisions on when to intervene, escalate, or authorize publication.
historic work: Key Activities - Edits, validates, markets and disseminates data.
change to work: This activity expands from direct dissemination of finished products to validating and overseeing automated dissemination pipelines and modular release components. 'Disseminates data' now includes assuring readiness of machine-actionable outputs, checking versioning and metadata completeness, supporting automated updates across channels, and intervening when automation produces errors, inconsistencies, or policy risks. Marketing-related activity also shifts toward ensuring discoverability and usability of open data, APIs, and dynamic dissemination products rather than primarily traditional publication formats.
justification: Human responsibility shifts toward oversight and exception handling where automation cannot fully resolve issues.

description: Skill in assessing client needs against available automated dissemination tools, APIs, reusable modules, and dynamic output options to reduce manual production and improve standardized delivery.
historic work: Key Activities - Interprets client information requests to create custom statistical tabulations.
change to work: Custom tabulation work is affected because dissemination increasingly occurs through modular, reusable, and automated components rather than bespoke one-off outputs. The officer will need to interpret whether a request can be met through existing APIs, open data endpoints, dynamic tables, or configurable dissemination modules before producing custom extracts. Complex user-specific requests may increasingly involve refining automated dissemination features or identifying exceptions where manual support remains necessary.
justification: The current role covers interpretation of requests and production of custom tabulations, but not evaluation of whether needs can be met through reusable automated dissemination services.

development area: API and open data delivery options
description: Knowledge of how users can access statistics through APIs, open data files, dynamic tables, and microdata access pathways, including limitations and appropriate use cases for each.
historic work: Key Activities - Interprets client information requests to create custom statistical tabulations.
change to work: Custom tabulation work is affected because dissemination increasingly occurs through modular, reusable, and automated components rather than bespoke one-off outputs. The officer will need to interpret whether a request can be met through existing APIs, open data endpoints, dynamic tables, or configurable dissemination modules before producing custom extracts. Complex user-specific requests may increasingly involve refining automated dissemination features or identifying exceptions where manual support remains necessary.
justification: The updated environment relies more on machine-accessible dissemination products and user-specific exception handling.

description: Skill in testing not only data quality but also output rendering, metadata integrity, API responses, update synchronization, and publication consistency across dissemination platforms.
historic work: Key Activities - Reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases.
change to work: Quality assessment extends beyond data values and database outputs to the performance and integrity of dissemination components themselves. The officer must assess whether automated dissemination modules correctly transform, version, label, and publish outputs across channels, including whether metadata, formatting, confidentiality controls, and update timing remain accurate and consistent.
justification: Current quality review is focused on systems and databases, but the update requires quality assurance of dissemination components, automated outputs, and cross-channel consistency.

description: Knowledge of how dissemination modules connect to upstream data sources and downstream delivery services, including interface dependencies, interoperability standards, and common failure points.
historic work: Key Activities - Reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases.
change to work: Quality assessment extends beyond data values and database outputs to the performance and integrity of dissemination components themselves. The officer must assess whether automated dissemination modules correctly transform, version, label, and publish outputs across channels, including whether metadata, formatting, confidentiality controls, and update timing remain accurate and consistent.
justification: Automation increases the need to understand how dissemination systems integrate with source systems and downstream services.
